units.title: Construct: Named interfaces, structural probes and semantic conformance
steps: Distinguish nominal registration, structural syntax compatibility and semantic interface laws; explain which C function-pointer mismatches need diagnostics and which wrong implementations still type-check.
Implement typed view constructors and a checked erased call wrapper with exactly-once callback invocation, stable table lifetime and failure-output staging.

Required rubric transfer: Implement struct ds_copy_view and ds_copy_checked from dispatch_laws.h under the shared cross-method contract. Use counted bytes of lengths0..16, including embedded zeros, and independently state the length/copy relation before building. The102 oracle rows combine length, two failure positions and false reported count. A deliberately zero-terminated length paired with counted copying compiles but fails for [1,0,2]. Preserve caller bytes/count on failure, invoke each admitted method once, and distinguish checked count agreement from uncheckable arbitrary callback behavior. D3 includes both semantic mutants plus actual Rust trait positive and negative controls: missing method and wrong signature reject, yet the Rust implementation with length1/copy3 compiles and runs. A method call without the extension trait in scope rejects separately. Explain why naming C free functions does not provide trait method lookup or coherence.
checks: A borrowed int7 measures7. A callback returning DS_FAILED after writing123 into its private output leaves caller output99 unchanged. A missing table rejects before invocation. The wrong-return-type callback fixture must fail strict C17 compilation.

Enumerate int values-8..8 and counted spans0..16; instrument callback count and outputs. Compile every diagnostic fixture separately under GCC/Clang -std=c17 -Wpedantic -Werror and retain the intended diagnostic. Wrong semantic callbacks must compile and be rejected by behavior/invariant checks, not by a cast or a runtime type-name string. Never execute a deliberately incompatible function-pointer call.

units.title: Construct: Fat views, embedded tables and unsafe qualifier substitution
steps: Derive the two representations and their table/data lifetime and cache costs; distinguish logical two-part dispatch from an ABI promise of exactly two machine words.
Implement an embedded-to-view adapter preserving concrete receiver address, const access and failure publication.

Required rubric transfer: Implement ds_multi_views for the two actual subobjects in struct ds_multi. Use every length0..16 and scalar value-16..16; mutate each after obtaining the views and verify the same views observe the corresponding live subobject. Replace the scalar table with the failing table and reconstruct the view; output must remain unchanged. Record actual sizeof/alignment/offsets and explain both owner and byte-array lifetime requirements. Neither mutant performs an invalid cast: one supplies the wrong valid interface, the other a stable unrelated integer. D3 also compares the actual Rust zero-sized marker and trait-reference observations with the C occupied marker/strict empty-struct diagnostic, and checks Rust's rejection of an escaping borrowed trait object. These are exact target/compiler observations, not an ABI or C borrow-checking guarantee.
checks: struct ds_box containing int17 measures17 through its embedded table. If its table returns DS_FAILED, output99 remains99. Assigning char** to const char** produces the intended diagnostic. A successful cast compilation is not permission to perform the counterfactual const write.

Compare outputs and failure side effects for every int-16..16 and both valid/failing tables. Measure sizeof/_Alignof/offsetof rather than assuming sizes. Analyze all three pointer levels in the qualifier fixture and keep diagnostics apart from runtime evidence. Rebuild both representations under GCC/Clang with and without link-time optimization; a compiler eliminating the indirect call is an observation for that build.
reasoning: A pair of pointers is an implementation choice, not a universal language ABI. Indirection changes where metadata lives, and apparently harmless qualifier widening can make a const object writable.
Derive the two representations and their table/data lifetime and cache costs; distinguish logical two-part dispatch from an ABI promise of exactly two machine words.
deliverables: Implement ds_embedded for struct ds_box and compare its in-object table with struct ds_view external table storage under the same measure contract. Construct arrays of1000 synthetic objects and1000 borrowed views, account for owner bytes versus view bytes and measure direct/embedded/fat calls with an equal workload. Compile the qualifier_reject.c fixture, then derive the counterfactual write that would become possible if T** could implicitly convert to const T**; analyze that write without executing it.
